result:
An overdue issue is announced by a background sweep, turned into one notification for its assignee, and shown or mailed according to that person's saved channels. Nothing on the issue page starts this.

## What starts the check

On a Node server, `register` in `src/instrumentation.ts` runs once before requests. It calls `registerEventHandlers` in `src/server/services/event-registry.ts`, then `startScheduler` in `src/server/jobs/scheduler.ts`. Importing the registry loads `src/server/services/notification-service.ts`, and that module's `registerFanOut` subscribes to `issue.overdue` before the scheduler is armed.

`startScheduler` sets a 60-second interval that calls `tick`. The timer is `unref`'d, and a second `startScheduler` call does nothing. `tick` walks `CADENCE_MINUTES`. `overdue-issues` is due on the first tick and again 60 minutes after `lastRunAt`. When it is due, `tick` calls `enqueue` in `src/server/jobs/queue.ts` with the id `overdue-issues:<minute bucket>`, then `drain`. `enqueue` ignores a duplicate id. `drain` takes due jobs oldest-first and `runHandler` dynamic-imports `runOverdueIssueJob`, passing a fresh `Date`.

The same function can also be started from outside the interval. `POST` in `src/app/api/cron/overdue/route.ts` calls `assertCronSecret` (header `x-taskflow-cron` must match `TASKFLOW_CRON_SECRET`) and then `runOverdueIssueJob(new Date())` directly. That route does not send mail. It only runs the scan, and the fan-out already attached in this process handles the event.

Opening an issue does not participate. `isOverdue` in `src/lib/date.ts` only paints due dates on cards and the due-date field.

## Which issues count

`runOverdueIssueJob` in `src/server/jobs/overdue-issue-job.ts` is wrapped by `runJob` from `src/server/jobs/types.ts`. It first calls `shouldFilterArchived` in `src/lib/soft-delete.ts` with an empty scope. An empty scope means "live rows only". If that ever returned false, the sweep logs and returns without scanning.

It then asks `listOrgIdsForRollup` in `src/server/repositories/usage-repository.ts` for 50 organization ids, oldest `measuredAt` first. Organizations with no usage row are absent. For each id, `listOverdueIssues` in `src/server/repositories/issue-repository.ts` keeps rows that are:

- in that organization (`orgPredicate`)
- live (`livePredicate` adds `archived_at IS NULL`)
- holding a due date (`dueAt` not null)
- already past the sweep timestamp (`dueAt < now`, ISO text compared with `lt`)
- still open: `backlog`, `todo`, `in_progress`, or `in_review`

`done` and `canceled` are the closed statuses in `CLOSED_ISSUE_STATUSES` in `src/types/issue.ts`, and they never come back. Results are ordered by `dueAt`. The query does not require an assignee. An unassigned overdue issue is still returned.

Inside the job, a null `dueAt` is skipped again, and any id already in the in-memory `reported` set is skipped. Everything else is announced.

## What the job owns

For each remaining issue it calls `emit` in `src/lib/event-bus.ts` with type `issue.overdue`. The payload, typed in `src/types/event.ts`, is the organization, `actorId: null`, the sweep time, the issue id, the project id, `dueAt`, and `assigneeId` (which may be null). On a resolved `emit` it adds the id to `reported` and increments `processed`. A throw increments `failed`, logs, and leaves the id out of `reported`.

`emit` waits for every subscriber with `Promise.allSettled` and does not rethrow a subscriber failure. A fan-out that rejects still counts as announced.

The job does not choose a recipient, read preferences, write a notification row, send mail, write an activity entry, or call a webhook. Activity, search, usage, and webhook listeners in `activity-service.ts`, `search-service.ts`, `usage-service.ts`, and `webhook-service.ts` do not subscribe to `issue.overdue`. The job's own comment states the split: it publishes the fact, and whoever cares reacts on the bus.

## Why the same issue is announced once

`reported` is a module-level `Set<string>` in `overdue-issue-job.ts`. A later sweep still finds the open, past-due issue, sees the id, and does not emit again. `resetOverdueTracking` clears that set for tests only.

The set lasts for the process lifetime. A restarted process starts empty and can announce again. Within one process, the scheduler also waits 60 minutes between `overdue-issues` runs, and a repeated cron call in that process hits the same set. The queue's retry (up to 5 attempts, then drop) only applies when `runHandler` throws. Per-issue failures are caught inside the job, so the queue treats that pass as finished.

## How that one person is told, on the channels they chose

`registerFanOut` handles `issue.overdue` by returning immediately when `assigneeId` is null. Otherwise it calls `notify` with kind `issue_overdue` and a recipient list of exactly that assignee. The title is "An issue is overdue", the body includes the issue id and `dueAt`, the href is `/issues/<issueId>`, and `actorId` is null. Because the actor is null, the "skip the person who caused it" rule in `notify` does not drop the assignee.

`notify` loads the organization, builds a `FlagContext` (plan and flag overrides, role null), and dedupes recipients. For the assignee it calls `getPreference` in `src/server/repositories/notification-preference-repository.ts` for `(orgId, userId, "issue_overdue")`. No row means the defaults in `notify`: `in_app` and `email`. A saved row goes through `resolveChannels`:

- `inApp` adds `in_app`.
- `email` adds `email` when the preference is not digest-only, or when it is digest-only and `isEnabled("digest_email", flags)` is true. That flag, in `src/config/feature-flags.ts`, requires the growth plan (or an override).
- An empty channel list writes no row.

`insertNotifications` in `src/server/repositories/notification-repository.ts` stores one row whose `recipientId` is the assignee and whose `channels` column is that JSON list.

Those choices are edited on `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/settings/notifications/page.tsx`. The page loads `listPreferences` for the signed-in user and renders `NotificationPreferencesForm`, which has an "Issue overdue" row with in-app, email, and (when `digest_email` is on) digest-only switches. Saving calls `updateNotificationPreferenceAction` in `src/actions/notifications/update-preferences.ts`, which rejects `digestOnly` when the flag is off, then `updatePreference`, which upserts through `upsertPreference`.

In the app, the row is read back only for that recipient. The dashboard layout calls `listNotifications` with `recipientId: actor.userId` and passes the unread total to `DashboardShell`, then `TopBar`, then `NotificationBell`. The inbox page and the `@panel/notifications` page call `listNotifications` the same way, after `can` allows `notification:read` on `notificationResource` for that user. `listNotifications` in the service checks `assertOrgScope` and `assertCan` before the repository filters `recipient_id`.

Email leaves later, and only for someone who opted into the digest. The same scheduler enqueues `digest-email` on a 60-minute cadence. `runDigestEmailJob` in `src/server/jobs/digest-email-job.ts` walks the same oldest-usage organization batch, keeps organizations whose `settings.digestHourUtc` equals the current UTC hour, and requires `digest_email`. `listDigestRecipients` returns users with any `digestOnly` preference. For each, `buildDigest` in `src/server/services/digest-service.ts` loads unread notifications since 24 hours ago via `listUnreadSince`, including this overdue row. `renderDigest` renders the `digest` template, `findUserById` supplies that user's address, and `sendEmail` in `src/server/services/email-service.ts` records the draft in the log (there is no outbound mail transport). The job then `markRead`s each digested row, so a later run in the same window does not send them again.
